key_insight: Allowing a Text-to-SQL agent to interact flexibly with the database—exploring schema structure and inspecting actual data values throughout planning and execution—lets it recover from early mistakes and produce more accurate, grounded SQL for large analytical databases.
problem_solved: Fixed, one-shot schema retrieval and post-hoc repair limit a system's ability to handle complex schemas, ambiguous user intents, and data-dependent grounding; FlexSQL addresses the need for iterative, data-aware decision making in Text-to-SQL agents.
method: Agent loop that alternates planning, targeted schema exploration, and lightweight data inspection rather than a single upfront retrieval step.
On-demand execution and partial runs to validate intermediate decisions against real data, enabling corrective steps before final SQL is produced.
Controller (LLM-based) that conditions generation on live database feedback, allowing dynamic recovery and refinement of queries.
impact: FlexSQL improves robustness and accuracy of Text-to-SQL on large, complex analytical databases, reducing error-prone outputs and developer effort; this enables more reliable natural-language access to real-world data for analytics and BI workflows.
visual_elements: Flow diagram of the FlexSQL agent loop: query → schema exploration → data inspection → partial execution → refinement → final SQL.
Side-by-side comparison: fixed-pipeline vs FlexSQL showing recovery from an initial mistake (error trace vs successful correction).
Schema map with highlighted exploration paths (tables/columns visited) to illustrate selective retrieval.
Bar chart or table summarizing accuracy/repair-rate improvements on complex analytical DB benchmarks.
paper_title: FlexSQL: Flexible Exploration and Execution Make Better Text-to-SQL Agents
paper_authors: Quang Hieu Pham, Yang He, Ping Nie, Canwen Xu, Davood Rafiei
